title: Multiply Strings
statement:
Multiply two non-negative integers that are given as decimal strings and return the product as a decimal string, without using big-number classes.

Contract
- `left` and `right` are non-null, non-empty, contain only the digits `0` to `9`, and have no leading zeros except for the single string `"0"`.
- Return the exact product as a string with no leading zeros; the product of anything with `"0"` is `"0"`.
- The inputs can be thousands of digits long, so do not convert them to `int`, `long`, `BigInteger` or `BigDecimal`.

Examples
- `multiply("12", "13")` returns `"156"`.
- `multiply("999", "999")` returns `"998001"`.
- `multiply("0", "5")` returns `"0"`.
hints: Do it the way you multiply on paper: every digit of one number meets every digit of the other.

A digit at position i of `left` and position j of `right` contributes to the result at positions i + j + 1 (the units) and i + j (the carry). Accumulate into an int array of length `left.length() + right.length()`.

Handle carries as you add each contribution, then skip leading zeros when building the string. Intended complexity: O(n * m) time for strings of length n and m and O(n + m) extra space; for equal lengths that is O(n^2) in the length.
inputSyntax: Input: two non-negative decimal numbers separated by a space, for example: 123 456
